title: CLI --run exits 0 on total failure (false success)
found_by: S3/S4/S5 C1 · S2 C1 · S1 A6
symptom: When the engine binary cannot be found, the shell still runs the command, fails with 127, and the CLI prints `# -> exit code 32512` while returning 0 to the OS. CI and automation see a green run.
root_cause: run_with_system() returns the raw system() wait status unmodified. Only the low 8 bits survive C process-exit truncation: 32512 = 127<<8 → 0. There is also no existence check on the engine before running.
evidence: Reproduced this pass (g++ 12.2). Relative settings path: `sh: …/examples/working_code/gifscythe/release/0.1.0/gifsicle: not found` then `# -> exit code 32512` then `echo $?` → 0. Same false-zero from /tmp with an absolute settings file that still string-sniffs a nested engine path.
fix: Pre-flight fs exists() on the engine and return 1. Decode wait status with WIFEXITED/WEXITSTATUS (or stop using system() entirely — see U-B6). Never return the raw wait status from main().

title: Engine path resolution works only by accident (CWD-dependent)
found_by: S3 C2 · S5 second pass · S2 C2 · S1 B4
symptom: Default engine path is working_code/gifscythe/release/0.1.0/gifsicle resolved against a 'repo root' discovered only when the settings path is absolute AND contains /working_code/gifscythe, or when CWD is the repo root. The product README's own usage from working_code/gifscythe fails.
root_cause: repo_root is derived by string-sniffing find(\/working_code/gifscythe\") + three-levels-of-parent fallback + CWD-relative probing. Three anchors that coincide for exactly one working directory. base_dir is only absolutized when it equals \".\"."
evidence: This pass: from product dir, `gifscythe-cli examples/animation.conf --run` looks for `examples/working_code/gifscythe/release/0.1.0/gifsicle` (not found, exit 0). From repo root with $PWD/…/animation.conf: engine found, writes /tmp/gifscythe_demo.gif 9458 bytes, exit 0.
fix: realpath the settings path at startup. Anchor engine search on the executable location (exe_dir/gifsicle, exe_dir/../release/<ver>/gifsicle), then GS_ENGINE, then PATH. Stop string-sniffing folder names.

title: GUI welds the queue into one GIF (Merge vs batch intent)
found_by: S3 C3 · S2 C3 · S1 B3
symptom: The UI presents an 'Animation queue' with 'Add GIF files…' — batch semantics — but every run hardcodes s.mode = gs::Mode::Merge. Queue two GIFs to optimize and the tool concatenates them into one animation.
root_cause: Merge was the CLI demo scenario (examples/animation.conf uses mode = merge). currentSettings() never reads a mode widget because none exists. gifsicle -m concatenates frame-by-frame.
evidence: This pass against the built engine: logo.gif = 12 images, logo1.gif = 1 image. `gifsicle -m -O3 logo.gif logo1.gif -o /tmp/merged.gif` → 13 images, logical screen 60x132. Silent data mangling of user intent.
fix: Default the queue to Mode::Batch (per-file, in-place or <name>_opt.gif). Keep Merge behind an explicit 'Merge into one animation' action. Add a mode combo (U-MISS-9).

title: Empty output path vaporizes the result, then reports success
found_by: S3 C4 · S2 C4 · S1 B2
symptom: The output field is optional (placeholder: 'Output file (optional)'). Left empty, gifsicle writes the optimized GIF to stdout. MainWindow never reads stdout. Status bar still says 'Optimization complete.'
root_cause: GifsicleCommand omits -o when output is empty (correct for the engine). runCommand() only calls readAllStandardError(). exitCode()==0 takes the success branch. The most common first run (add a GIF, click Optimize, skip output) is guaranteed data loss.
evidence: This pass: `gifsicle -O3 logo1.gif | wc -c` → 821. MainWindow.cpp:131 is the only read. No readAllStandardOutput(), no QFileInfo existence check after the run.
fix: Refuse empty output, or auto-derive <input>_opt.gif in batch mode. After a normal exit, verify the output file exists and size>0 before claiming success.

title: waitForFinished() timeout ignored → zombie process + wrong status
found_by: S3 G4 · S2 N15 · S1 A3
symptom: proc.waitForFinished(60000) blocks the UI thread up to 60s; its bool return is ignored. On timeout the process is still running, but exitStatus()/exitCode() on a live QProcess default to NormalExit/0, so the UI can report success for a process that has not finished. The QProcess destructor then kills it.
root_cause: Synchronous QProcess on the GUI thread with discarded timeout. Large animations — the app's entire reason to exist — exceed 60s routinely.
evidence: Source: line 130 calls waitForFinished(60000) with no if. Lines 132–137 branch only on exitStatus/exitCode. QProcess docs: those getters are 0/NormalExit while Running.
fix: Check the bool; on timeout proc.kill() and report failure. Real fix is async member QProcess with finished/readyReadStandardError, progress, and cancel (U-MISS-4).

title: Shell execution of a concatenated command string (spaces + injection)
found_by: S3 G3 · S2 G3 · S1 A6
symptom: toString() joins argv with bare spaces (no quoting). The CLI executes that string through std::system(). Any path with a space breaks. Any settings value with shell metacharacters is interpreted by /bin/sh. Power users copy the unquoted line from the live pane into a terminal and it fails the same way.
root_cause: Display string and execution string are the same object. argv already exists on GifsicleCommand but --run never uses args(); it concatenates engine_path + ' ' + cli and hands it to the shell.
evidence: toString() loop is `if (i) o << ' '; o << args_[i];` — zero quoting helpers in the file (confirmed grep). CLI: `std::string full = engine_path + \ \" + cli; run_with_system(full);`. GUI is safer here: QProcess setArguments uses argv
fix: so this critical is CLI+display."
phase: Execute via posix_spawn/execvp (CreateProcess on Windows) using args(). Add shell_quote() used only by toString() for the live pane.

title: CMake cannot configure: header-only lib declared STATIC
found_by: S3 M2 · S2 M2 · S1 A2
symptom: cmake generation fails: Cannot determine link language for target gifscythe_core. Linux CI still looks green because build.sh prefers qmake and swallows cmake stderr.
root_cause: A STATIC library needs ≥1 compiled translation unit. target_sources(... PRIVATE src/core/SettingsIO.h) contributes only a header. cmake is not installed in this sandbox so configure was not re-run here; the CMakeLists block is verbatim.
evidence: CMakeLists.txt lines 8–12: add_library(gifscythe_core STATIC) + SettingsIO.h only. build.sh:62–63 runs cmake … >/dev/null 2>&1. This sandbox: cmake: command not found, so V1 for the source defect, V2 for the historical CMake 3.30.2 transcript.
fix: add_library(gifscythe_core INTERFACE) with INTERFACE includes. Stop silencing cmake. When --all is requested and the GUI cannot build, exit non-zero.

title: Windows CI: wrong package name + missing GUI/deploy steps
symptom: Windows job dies at Qt install. Even a correct install would not build the GUI: the job runs bare ./build.sh, which forces want_gui=0. No windeployqt, no artifact, engine built twice.
root_cause: Three stacked defects: (1) choco install qt6-base — Linux job correctly uses apt qt6-base-dev; Windows uses a name that does not exist on Chocolatey. (2) bare ./build.sh never builds GUI (U-B9.3). (3) no PATH to Qt, no cmake GUI step, no windeployqt, no upload-artifact. Plus NEW-1: even a green install still cannot compile the engine with the Linux config.h.
evidence: build.yml:28 `choco install qt6-base mingw`. build.yml:38 `./build.sh`. build.sh:34–36 want_gui=auto forced to 0. No windeployqt anywhere in the repo (grep).
fix: aqtinstall or jurplel/install-qt-action; build engine once with a Windows config; build CLI+tests; cmake GUI + windeployqt; upload artifact; run test_engine.sh. Do not use choco qt6-base.

title: build.sh GUI dispatch: three logic errors
symptom: Header comment promises GUI 'only where Qt6 is installed'. Default ./build.sh never builds it. --gui still builds engine+tests. cmake-success can still print 'GUI build failed' because the next block insists on qmake6.
root_cause: (1) cmake path sets qt_found=1 then the qmake6 block runs anyway. (2) --gui does not skip steps 1–3. (3) want_gui=auto is immediately forced to 0. Also: cmake detection actually builds as a side effect of 'checking' for cmake, and $root is computed and never used.
evidence: build.sh:6 header vs :34–36 force-0. :7 '--gui skip engine/tests' vs :38–51 always run. :60–73 cmake then qmake. :26 root= unused.
fix: One honest GUI branch: qmake6 → qmake → cmake, report truthfully, exit non-zero if GUI was requested but unbuilt. Align the header with the code.

title: Uninitialized reads on malformed settings (undefined behavior)
found_by: S3 C5 · S2 C5 · S1 A7
symptom: lossy = abc (and optimize = xyz) emit --lossy=0 -O0 with no warning. On other compilers the indeterminate long can be any value; an in-range garbage color count would pass GifsicleCommand range checks silently.
root_cause: `long v; i >> v; return v;` — if extraction fails, v is indeterminate. Same for to_double. No load-warning channel.
evidence: This pass: a conf with lossy=abc optimize=xyz colors=999 produced `…gifsicle -m --lossy=0 -O0 /tmp/nope.gif -o /tmp/out.gif` (colors dropped: U-MISS-2). A probe program printed to_long(\abc\")=0
fix: to_double(\"abc\")=0 on gcc 12.2 — the 'lucky zero' the forensic audit observed."
phase: Initialize v=0, return bool from to_long/to_double, keep the default and surface a load warning. Clamp parsed values to legal ranges (U-MISS-2).

title: Version 'single source of truth' hardcoded in many places
files: VERSION.md, CMakeLists.txt, gifscythe.pro, qtui/main.cpp, MainWindow.cpp, cli/main.cpp, test_engine.sh, GifsicleSettings.h, build_gifsicle.sh fallback

title: 'Add GIF files…' replaces the queue instead of appending
symptom: Second selection throws away the first. Opposite of every batch queue (XnConvert, Caesium) the vision cites.

title: The 'live' command pane isn't live
symptom: Hint label: 'The command preview is always kept in sync.' Only the two spinboxes are connected to refreshCommand(). Typing in the output field does not update the pane until Browse is used.
root_cause: connect() only on optimizeSpin_ and lossySpin_ valueChanged. outputEdit_ has no textChanged. Queue changes refresh only because chooseInputs calls refreshCommand() after replace.

fix: Connect outputEdit_::textChanged and the list model. Better: one settingsChanged() signal every control emits. Quote args for display (U-MISS-3).

title: build.sh docs promise a GUI the default path never builds
symptom: Header: '+ GUI (only where Qt6 is installed)'. Code: want_gui=auto immediately becomes 0. SESSION_HANDOFF treats the build script as the contract with the next session.
root_cause: Comment written for the intended behavior; the auto branch was disabled and never updated.
evidence: build.sh:6 vs :34–36.

title: Dead config.h writer + swallowed Qt-build errors
symptom: build_gifsicle.sh announces 'writing a generated one' and writes nothing. build.sh sends the entire Qt build to /dev/null, then says 'see Qt errors above' when none are visible.

evidence: build_gifsicle.sh:57–61 if [[ ! -f config.h ]] echo … fi with no redirect/write. build.sh:70–73 qmake6 … >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo GUI build failed (see Qt errors above).
fix: Delete the dead branch; comment that config.h is the handwritten Linux file in reference_code/gifsicle/. Log Qt output to a file and tail it on failure.

title: Packagers look for the GUI where cmake does not put it
symptom: cmake emits the GUI into build/, qmake into build/gui/. Both packaging scripts only copy build/gui/gifscythe. A 'portable GUI release' can silently ship without the GUI. windeployqt is manual-only.
root_cause: Two build systems, one packager assumption.
evidence: package_portable.sh:12 `build/gui/gifscythe`. CMake qt_add_executable(gifscythe …) with no RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY set to build/gui.
fix: One build path (CMake), one output dir. package_portable.sh runs windeployqt on Windows. CI asserts expected files exist in the portable folder.

title: Engine identity vs product identity conflated
symptom: gifsicle --version reports 'LCDF Gifsicle 0.1.0' instead of 1.96. Engine version ≠ product version; upstream traceability is lost.
root_cause: COMPILE_ARGS uses -DVERSION=\\\$VERSION\\\" where VERSION is grepped from the product VERSION.md."
evidence: This pass after a successful native engine build: first line of --version is exactly `LCDF Gifsicle 0.1.0`. Copyright still 1997-2025 Eddie Kohler.
fix: Keep -DVERSION=\\\1.96\\\" for the engine. Use the product version only for the release directory name."

title: Settings parser inconsistencies
symptom: Bool parsing is inconsistent: info accepts 1/true/yes, every other bool only 1/true. (unsigned)to_long wraps negatives silently to huge crop/position values.
root_cause: Copy-paste of ad-hoc parsers. No parse_bool(), no range check before the unsigned cast.
evidence: This pass probe: info=yes → 1, interlace=yes → 0. to_long(\-5\")=-5
fix: (unsigned) that is 4294967291. Original note that rotation has no 'none': actually any unrecognized value including 'none' falls through to Rotation::None — so 'none' works by accident. Partial on that sub-claim."
phase: One parse_bool() that accepts 1/true/yes/on. Reject/clamp negatives before unsigned casts. Treat unknown rotation explicitly.

title: Doc & repo hygiene drift
symptom: Root README layout block still says gifsicle-1.96/ as the repo root folder name. .gitignore ignores release/*/gifsicle but not packaged Gifscythe* folders. Qt6-deprecated QStringList::toStdVector/fromStdVector still used. Two parallel build systems.
root_cause: Docs written against an older tree shape; Qt API used from memory of Qt5.
evidence: Root README.md line 8 of the layout fence is `gifsicle-1.96/`. MainWindow.cpp:109 toStdVector, :125 fromStdVector. No root .gitignore at all (this pass) — stronger than the original note.
fix: Fix the folder name, ignore packaged folders, replace deprecated Qt APIs with range constructors, standardize on CMake.

title: SettingsIO cannot save — 'load/save' is load-only
symptom: The header describes itself as the load/save serialization the GUI will use to persist per-file settings and round-trip state. There is no writer. No presets, no per-file persistence, no CLI↔GUI round-trip.
root_cause: Writer never implemented. load_settings_file even swallows open failures and returns a default Settings.
evidence: This pass: grep save_settings over working_code/gifscythe → no matches. Header comment line 1–3 still says 'Load/save'.
fix: save_settings() as the exact inverse of load_settings() plus a round-trip unit test load(save(s)) == s.

title: No validation layer — bad values vanish silently
symptom: Out-of-range settings are dropped without a trace. colors=999 emits no -k. disposal=9 emits nothing. In a GUI, a control that 'does nothing' is indistinguishable from a bug.
root_cause: GifsicleCommand gates on ranges (color_count 2–256, disposal 0–7) and simply omits the flag. No Warning type, no CLI print, no GUI hint.
evidence: This pass: conf with colors=999 produced a command with no -k. lossy=abc became --lossy=0 via U-B10 rather than a parse error.
fix: gs::validate(const Settings&) → vector<Warning>{field,value,reason}. CLI prints them. GUI shows inline hints.

title: No safe-execution layer / no shell quoting / no ~ expansion
symptom: Execution uses a shell (U-B6). Display is unquoted. resolve_path() treats leading ~ as 'absolute' and returns it unchanged, so the engine receives a literal tilde.
root_cause: resolve_path: `if (p.empty() || p[0]=='/' || p[0]=='~') return p;`
evidence: cli/main.cpp:44. No tilde expansion, no $HOME. toString has no quote helper.
fix: argv exec + shell_quote for display. Expand ~ to $HOME or reject with a clear error.

title: GUI: no async execution, no progress, no cancel
symptom: WORKLIST task 4 (progress, cancel) has no foundation. Run blocks the UI thread. runButton_ stays enabled because the event loop is frozen, then a timeout can lie (U-B5).
root_cause: QProcess is a stack local inside runCommand(), not a member, so signals cannot outlive the call.
evidence: MainWindow.h has no QProcess member (only an unused #include <QProcess>). runCommand constructs `QProcess proc(this)` on the stack.
fix: Member QProcess, started/readyReadStandardError/finished, busy state disabling Run, Cancel → kill(). Per-file progress in batch mode.

title: No shared engine discovery / startup health check
symptom: CLI and GUI each invented their own locator. CLI is CWD-sniffed (U-B2). GUI only looks at applicationDirPath()/gifsicle — which is never where build.sh puts the engine (release/<ver>/).
root_cause: No gs::EngineLocator in core. GUI line 26 is a one-liner with no fallback and no .exe suffix (see NEW-2).
evidence: GUI: `enginePath_ = QCoreApplication::applicationDirPath() + \/gifsicle\";` — no exists() check at startup
fix: no release/ probe
sort_order: gs::EngineLocator in src/core (exe-dir → GS_ENGINE → PATH → release/<GS_VERSION>), used by both fronts. Show path+version in the GUI status bar.

title: Tests never exercise the flows that actually fail
symptom: 35 in-process argv assertions on happy paths. Nothing covers --run exit codes, CWD sensitivity, merge-vs-batch, empty output, malformed conf, spaces in paths, or SettingsIO round-trip. test_engine.sh is not called by build.sh or CI.
root_cause: Unit tests were written against the command builder only. IMPROVEMENT_LOG's 'integration tests pass' has no integration test.
evidence: This pass: 35 CHECK() calls + 1 macro (grep CHECK( = 36). test_engine.sh 5/5 pass when invoked by hand. grep test_engine in build.sh and build.yml → no matches. Test 4 is also tautological (NEW-15).
fix: CI smoke: --run from ≥2 CWDs, malformed-conf, merge-vs-batch, spaces-in-paths, SettingsIO round-trip, test_engine.sh both jobs, artifact upload.

title: Drag-and-drop: enabled but not implemented
symptom: inputList_->setAcceptDrops(true) with no dragEnterEvent/dropEvent override. Dropping files from the OS does nothing (QListWidget default DnD is internal item moves).
root_cause: Flag set as a TODO marker. WORKLIST task 4 still open.
evidence: Line 44 is the only drop-related call. MainWindow does not override drop events. No custom QListWidget subclass.
fix: Subclass QListWidget or event-filter; accept Qt::CopyAction; append mimeData()->urls() with dedupe.

title: No queue management controls
symptom: No Remove-Selected, no Clear-All. Combined with U-M2 (replace-not-append), users restart the app to drop one file.
root_cause: MVP scaffold only wired Add.
evidence: Left column widgets: label, QListWidget, one 'Add GIF files…' button. No other queue actions.
fix: Remove-Selected + Clear-All. Already on WORKLIST task 4.

title: No mode selector — Batch/Explode/Auto unreachable in the GUI
symptom: Mode::Merge is hardcoded. Mode::Batch, Explode, Auto exist in the core layer and settings format but no widget exposes them. This is why U-B3 happens.
root_cause: GUI MVP only exposed optimize + lossy + output.
evidence: currentSettings(): `gs::Settings s; s.mode = gs::Mode::Merge;`. No QComboBox in the file.
fix: QComboBox Auto/Merge/Batch/Explode. Required once U-B3 is fixed so the user can choose 'optimize each' vs 'merge into one'.

title: Dither is bool-only; docs promise method selection
symptom: FEASIBILITY_REVIEW mapping table says --dither=floyd-steinberg|ro64|none. Core models bool dither and emits bare -f (default Floyd–Steinberg).
root_cause: MVP mapped the short option only. Committed engine: -f is a separate flag; --dither is Clp_ValString with Clp_Optional, so methods need the attached form.
evidence: gifsicle.c options[]: `{ 0, 'f', DITHER_OPT, 0, Clp_Negate }` and `{ \dither\"
column17: Clp_Negate | Clp_Optional }`. Code emitting -f is correct as far as it goes."

title: No LICENSE / GPL compliance artifacts in the product tree
symptom: FEASIBILITY_REVIEW §5 is explicit: distributing gifsicle (GPL v2-only) alongside a GPLv3 UI requires shipping gifsicle's license text + source offer. There is no LICENSE/COPYING at repo root. package_portable.sh ships VERSION.md + README.md only.
root_cause: Compliance deferred. Engine COPYING exists only under reference_code/gifsicle/COPYING — the packager never copies it.
evidence: This pass find LICENSE/COPYING at depth≤3: only the two gifsicle trees. package_portable.sh:13 copies VERSION.md README.md.
fix: Add COPYING (GPLv2 for the engine) + attribution; copy them into the portable folder; keep gifsicle a separate process forever unless Eddie Kohler grants a v3 exception.

title: Windows packaging path incomplete
symptom: No windeployqt automation, no Windows GUI build in CI, no artifact, no smoke test of the portable folder on a clean machine. This is the whole remaining path to 1.0.0.
root_cause: Packaging scripts were written on Linux against the qmake output layout.
evidence: grep windeployqt over the repo: no matches except docs. Windows job has no upload-artifact.
fix: windeployqt inside package_portable.sh on Windows; CI asserts portable-folder contents; clean-machine smoke test before 1.0.0.

title: Remaining GifsicleSettings controls unexposed in GUI
symptom: The GUI exposes 2 of ~30 modeled controls (optimize + lossy; output is a path, not a gifsicle feature). FEASIBILITY_REVIEW §3(2) already contains the complete slider↔flag mapping table.
root_cause: Planned retrofit, not an accident — listed for completeness so it does not get lost behind 'MVP done'.
evidence: Settings has mode, info, interlace, flips, rotation, position, crop, delay, disposal, loopcount, unoptimize, threads, colors, dither, gamma, color_method, careful, resize_*, background, transparent, comments, explode_by_name. GUI binds optimize_level, lossy, output, inputs.
fix: Mechanical widgets↔settings work on top of the now-honest core. Keep the live raw-CLI pane. After P0/P1, not before.

title: REFUTED — loopcount=0 is not 'play once'
symptom: Secondary audit claimed --loopcount=0 emits the wrong flag and should be changed to --loopcount=forever. Implementing that 'fix' is unnecessary; changing the semantics would be the bug.
root_cause: Misread of the man page. --loopcount=0 is equivalent to --loopcount=forever, not --no-loopcount.
evidence: This pass, committed source gifsicle.c case 'l': if negated, loopcount=-1 (--no-loopcount); else loopcount = (clp->have_val ? clp->val.i : 0). Official man page: '--loopcount=0 is equivalent to --loopcount=forever, not --no-loopcount.' Current code emitting --loopcount=0 for 'loop forever' is exactly right.
fix: Do not change this. Both forms work; =0 is canonical. Keep the unit test that asserts --loopcount=0.

title: REFUTED — -O0 is valid ('optimization off')
symptom: Secondary audit claimed -O0 is invalid and the spinbox should clamp to 1. The GUI already exposes 0–3. Clamping to 1 would remove a legitimate 'off' setting.
root_cause: Man page lists three positive levels; the parser still accepts 0 and uses it to clear the optimize mask.
evidence: This pass, OPTIMIZE_OPT handler: if negated or value<0 then o=0; else o = have_val ? val.i : 1; then `optimizing = (optimizing & ~GT_OPT_MASK) | o`. No error path for 0. GUI spinbox range 0–3 is correct; label 0 as 'Off' if anything.
fix: Do not clamp. Optionally setSpecialValueText('Off') on optimizeSpin_ like lossy already does.

title: REFUTED — MainWindow.h missing from CMake does not break moc
symptom: Secondary audit claimed omitting MainWindow.h from target sources causes a linker 'undefined reference to vtable'.
root_cause: qt_standard_project_setup() (Qt ≥ 6.3) sets CMAKE_AUTOMOC ON. AUTOMOC scans headers included by listed sources — MainWindow.h is #included by MainWindow.cpp. qmake path mocs Q_OBJECT headers automatically too.
evidence: CMakeLists.txt calls qt_standard_project_setup() then qt_add_executable(gifscythe src/qtui/main.cpp src/qtui/MainWindow.cpp). Weakest grade: not execution-verified here (no Qt in this sandbox). Adding the header to sources remains a harmless belt-and-braces measure.
fix: No link failure to fix. Optional: list MainWindow.h in target sources for older Qt.

title: REFUTED — gamma does not default to 0.0
symptom: Secondary audit claimed gamma defaults to 0.0 so --gamma 0.0 is always emitted. That would have been a real bug. It is not the code.
root_cause: Misread of the default. Sentinel is -1.0; gate is >= 0.
evidence: This pass, GifsicleSettings.h: `double gamma = -1.0; // --gamma; -1 = unchanged`. GifsicleCommand.h: `if (s.gamma >= 0) { add --gamma; add f2s(s.gamma); }`. --gamma is Clp_ValString (required value), so the two-arg form is also correct.
fix: No change. Do not implement the attached audit's P1 'Fix Argument Logic (N1, N2, N14)' — all three premises are wrong.

title: Windows engine is compiled against Linux config.h — static_assert will fire
symptom: Even after U-B8 (Chocolatey package name) is fixed, `./scripts/build_gifsicle.sh --windows` still feeds the handwritten Linux config.h to a Win64 compiler. gifsicle.c main() static_assert(sizeof(unsigned long) == SIZEOF_UNSIGNED_LONG) will fail: Win64 long is 4 bytes, config.h says 8. PATHNAME_SEPARATOR is '/', RANDOM is random() (win32cfg.h correctly has '\\\\' and rand). The dedicated win32cfg.h is never included.
root_cause: build_gifsicle.sh always compiles with -DHAVE_CONFIG_H -I. using reference_code/gifsicle/config.h, for both native and --windows. The 'if no config.h, writing a generated one' branch is dead (U-M5) and would still write the Linux file. Upstream split Makefile.w32 / Makefile.w64 exists for this exact reason — the comment above the static_assert says so.
evidence: config.h:56 `#define SIZEOF_UNSIGNED_LONG 8`, :61 PATHNAME_SEPARATOR '/', :39 `#define RANDOM random`. win32cfg.h:137 SIZEOF_UNSIGNED_LONG 4, :125 PATHNAME_SEPARATOR '\\\\', :128 RANDOM rand. gifsicle.c:1462–1468 comment: 'If these assertions fail, you've used the wrong Makefile. You should've used Makefile.w32 for 32-bit Windows and Makefile.w64 for 64-bit Windows.' quantize.c calls RANDOM(). build_gifsicle.sh uses the same COMPILE_ARGS for TARGET=windows and native.
fix: For --windows, copy/adapt win32cfg.h as config.h (or -include src/win32cfg.h and do not include the Linux config.h). Set SIZEOF_UNSIGNED_LONG 4, SIZEOF_VOID_P 8, PATHNAME_SEPARATOR '\\\\', RANDOM rand, drop HAVE_UNISTD_H / HAVE_MKSTEMP / HAVE_SYS_SELECT_H as needed. Do not share the Linux config.h across targets.

title: GUI engine locator cannot find the engine in the default build layout
symptom: GUI sets enginePath_ to applicationDirPath()/gifsicle once in the constructor and never probes anywhere else. build.sh puts the engine at release/<ver>/gifsicle and the GUI at build/gui/gifscythe (qmake) or build/gifscythe (cmake). Those directories are not the same. On Windows the binary is gifsicle.exe and the locator does not append .exe. First-run GUI users always hit 'Could not start gifsicle' unless they manually copy the engine beside the GUI — which the packager also fails to do for .exe (NEW-5).
root_cause: A one-line absolute-looking path that is actually layout-relative and platform-naive. No startup exists() check, so the failure is deferred to Run.
evidence: MainWindow.cpp:26 is the only assignment to enginePath_. No other search. package_portable.sh copies `release/$version/gifsicle` (no .exe) next to a GUI that looks for `./gifsicle`. On a Linux qmake build the GUI lives in build/gui/, engine in release/0.1.0/.
fix: Same EngineLocator as U-MISS-5, with .exe on Windows. At startup, if not found, disable Run and put the missing path in the status bar instead of 'Ready'.

title: FEASIBILITY promised a two-way live CLI pane — reverse parser does not exist
symptom: The architecture review that the project treats as law says: 'a live raw-CLI pane that two-way syncs with the widgets (change a slider → the CLI text updates; edit the CLI text → the widgets update). Power users get 100% of the tool.' The pane is read-only (setReadOnly(true)), one-way, and not even fully one-way (U-M3). There is no argv→Settings parser at all.
root_cause: MVP implemented Settings→argv (GifsicleCommand) and stopped. The reverse direction was the actual 'retain terminal control' feature.
evidence: FEASIBILITY_REVIEW.md: 'exposing a live raw-CLI pane that two-way syncs with the widgets'. MainWindow.cpp:76 commandPane_->setReadOnly(true). No parse_command() / fromArgs() anywhere in src/core.
fix: After P0 honesty work: either (a) keep the pane read-only and change the docs/label so they stop promising two-way, or (b) add gs::parse_args() and make the pane editable. Do not ship 1.0.0 claiming two-way if it is (a).

title: Delay unit trap: FEASIBILITY maps 'ms' onto gifsicle -d (centiseconds)
symptom: The mapping table the UI/UX retrofit is supposed to follow says 'Per-frame delay (ms)' → `-d`. gifsicle -d is in 1/100 second, not milliseconds. A slider labelled milliseconds that writes delay_cs will make every animation 10× too slow. Core currently names the field delay_cs — the trap is in the doc the next session is told to implement.
root_cause: Feasibility table written from memory of 'delay is a time' without checking the man page unit.
evidence: GifsicleSettings.h: `int delay_cs = -1; // -d, in 1/100 sec`. animation.conf `delay = 5` (50 ms). gifsicle.1 and options[]: `{ \delay\"
column18: Correct the mapping table now. GUI label must say 'Delay (1/100 s)' or convert ms÷10 with a visible note. Add a unit test that delay=5 emits `-d 5`, not 50.

title: Packagers never copy gifsicle.exe — Windows portable folder is engine-less
symptom: build_gifsicle.sh --windows writes release/<ver>/gifsicle.exe. package_portable.sh requires `-x release/<ver>/gifsicle` (no .exe) and copies that. On Windows the test fails and the script exits 1, or if someone renamed the file, the GUI still looks for `gifsicle` (NEW-2). The portable Windows story WORKLIST calls 'the path to 1.0.0' cannot succeed with these scripts as written.
root_cause: Scripts are Linux-only in their binary names despite the product being Windows-first (PROJECT_VISION).
evidence: build_gifsicle.sh:31 EXE=gifsicle.exe for windows, :34 EXE=gifsicle otherwise. package_portable.sh:7 `engine=.../gifsicle` then :9 `[[ -x $engine ]] || exit 1`. package_system.sh loops the same nameless-exe path.
fix: Probe gifsicle then gifsicle.exe. Copy whichever exists. GUI locator must match. Add a CI assertion that the portable folder contains the engine AND the GUI on Windows.

title: GifsicleCommand stores a const Settings& — temporaries dangle
symptom: `GifsicleCommand cmd(currentSettings()); cmd.toString();` is undefined behavior: currentSettings() returns by value, the temporary is bound in the ctor, then destroyed, leaving settings_ dangling. Current call sites happen to use named locals so they are safe. The type is a landmine for the GUI retrofit (every new widget helper will be tempted to write the temporary form).
root_cause: Header-only builder kept a reference to avoid copying a struct with vectors. Lifetime was never part of the contract.
evidence: GifsicleCommand.h: `explicit GifsicleCommand(const Settings& s) : settings_(s) {}` and `const Settings& settings_;`. MainWindow currently does `const auto settings = currentSettings(); GifsicleCommand cmd(settings);` — safe by accident. No value/move ctor.
fix: Store Settings by value (it is small). Or take Settings by value in the ctor. Add a unit test that constructs from a prvalue and reads args().

title: SettingsIO uses std::tolower without <cctype>; CLI uses istringstream without <sstream>
symptom: Both compile on this libstdc++ only because of transitive includes. A different standard library, or a future header cleanup, breaks the CLI and the parser. This is the kind of 'green on my machine' defect the project already has too many of.
root_cause: Headers relied on whatever <string>/<fstream> pulled in.
evidence: SettingsIO.h includes fstream, sstream, string, vector — not cctype — then `std::tolower((unsigned char)c)`. cli/main.cpp includes SettingsIO.h, GifsicleCommand.h, cstdio, cstring, cstdlib, string, vector, unistd.h — not sstream — then `std::istringstream iss(content);`. Both compiled clean with -Wall -Wextra -pedantic here via transitive includes.
fix: Include what you use: <cctype> in SettingsIO.h, <sstream> (and drop unistd.h behind a POSIX guard) in main.cpp.

title: 74 MB Caesium binary bundle committed; no root .gitignore; duplicate gifsicle trees
symptom: FEASIBILITY_REVIEW says adapt Caesium from source, not binaries, and notes the GPL-v3 vs gifsicle GPL-v2-only conflict. The repo nevertheless ships the full Caesium 2.8.5 Windows app (Caesium Image Compressor.exe + Qt6 DLLs, 74 MB, 62 files). A second full gifsicle 1.96 tree (gifsicle-nested-1.96) duplicates reference_code/gifsicle. No root .gitignore, so future clones of caesium-source/ and gifsicle-upstream/ will be tempting to commit. Repo is 106 MB for a 0.1.0 skeleton.
root_cause: Reference material was copied in wholesale. SESSION_HANDOFF says reference_code is read-only; it does not say 'do not ship someone else's product'.
evidence: du: caesium-bin 74M, gifsicle 1.3M, gifsicle-nested-1.96 1.3M, whole clone 106M. git ls-files caesium-bin | wc -l → 62. ls root .gitignore → not found. FEASIBILITY: 'Caveat A — no source in the repo: To adapt the GUI you must start from Caesium's source, not the binaries.'
fix: Gitignore caesium-bin or replace with a README pointer. Drop gifsicle-nested-1.96 unless a diff against gifsicle/ is documented. Add a root .gitignore for reference clones, build trees, and portable folders. Do not redistribute Caesium's packaged app.

symptom: Comment: 'Make base_dir absolute so it works regardless of CWD.' Implementation: only if base_dir == \.\". For the documented `examples/animation.conf`
root_cause: base_dir stays the relative string `examples`

title: Include-guard typo GIFSYCYTHE (missing C) in every header
symptom: Guards are GIFSYCYTHE_CORE_* / GIFSYCYTHE_MAINWINDOW_H. Harmless today, but a later 'fix the typo in one header' creates a second include of the same file under a new guard — ODR / redefinition hell during the retrofit.
root_cause: Product name Gifscythe, guard written as Gifsycthe.
evidence: All four headers. Settings.h:12 `#ifndef GIFSYCYTHE_CORE_GIFSICLE_SETTINGS_H`.
fix: Rename to GIFSCYTHE_* in one commit, all headers together.

title: test_engine.sh ((PASS++)) is a set -e landmine; no .gitattributes for *.sh
symptom: ok() does `((PASS++))`. When PASS is 0 the arithmetic expression evaluates to 0, so the command's exit status is 1. The script currently uses `set -uo pipefail` without -e, so it survives. The moment someone 'fixes' the script by adding -e (or sources it from a stricter runner), the first passing test aborts the suite with a false failure. Also no .gitattributes to force LF on *.sh — CRLF checkout on Windows breaks shebangs.
root_cause: Classic bash ((var++)) pitfall. Unix scripts committed without eol normalization.
evidence: test_engine.sh:10 `set -uo pipefail`. :28 `ok() { echo \  PASS: $1\"; ((PASS++)); }`. This pass the suite printed 5 passed / 0 failed because -e is off. No .gitattributes in the clone."
fix: ok() { echo …; PASS=$((PASS+1)); } or `((++PASS))`. Add `set -e` only after that. Add `.gitattributes` with `*.sh text eol=lf`.

title: CLI is POSIX-only: unistd.h, '/', getcwd — Windows paths treated as relative
symptom: PROJECT_VISION: Windows-first. CLI includes <unistd.h>, splits on '/', treats p[0]=='/' as the only absolute-path test. A settings path `C:\\…\\animation.conf` is 'relative'. Drive-letter engine paths never match `engine_path[0] != '/'`. MinGW may compile it; MSVC will not. Combined with NEW-1/NEW-5 the Windows CLI story has no working path.
root_cause: CLI written on Linux as a proof and never ported, despite being the 'power-user terminal interface' the GUI pane is supposed to match.
evidence: main.cpp:21 `#include <unistd.h>`. :44 `p[0]=='/'`. :74 `find_last_of('/')`. :93 `settings_path[0]=='/'`. :109 `engine_path[0] != '/'`. No _fullpath, no std::filesystem, no wchar API.
fix: Use std::filesystem::path everywhere (C++17 is already the project standard). exists(), absolute(), parent_path(). Drop unistd.h. This also fixes NEW-9.

symptom: The mapping table writes `--crop X,Y,WxH` (comma before size). gifsicle wants `--crop X,Y+WIDTHxHEIGHT` (plus form). The code already emits `0,0+30x60` and the unit test asserts that. A well-meaning retrofit that 'aligns code to the table' would generate a flag gifsicle rejects.
root_cause: Feasibility table approximated the man page. Code was checked against the engine.
evidence: Unit test 5: CHECK(has(args, \0
fix: 0+30x60\")). GifsicleCommand build() concatenates x

column18: Edit the table, not the emitter. Same discipline as the N1/N2/N14 refutations: do not change correct code to match a wrong document.

title: Named --gamma values (srgb|oklab) from the mapping table are unmodeled
symptom: FEASIBILITY maps 'Gamma / color math' to `--gamma=srgb|oklab|NUM`. Core stores a double and emits `--gamma <float>` as two arguments. srgb/oklab cannot be expressed. Also f2s() uses default ostream precision, so 2.2 may round-trip as 2.2000000000000002.
root_cause: Numeric-only field. Engine option is Clp_ValString, so named gammas are legal.
evidence: gifsicle.c: `{ \gamma\"

title: CMake build_engine custom target invokes a bash script (broken on Windows cmd)
symptom: add_custom_target(build_engine COMMAND ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/scripts/build_gifsicle.sh) with no interpreter. On a Windows CMake GUI build (the path U-B8's fix will use) this target cannot run unless the generator happens to be bash. USES_TERMINAL does not supply bash.
root_cause: Linux-only hook left as a convenience.
evidence: CMakeLists.txt:43–46 verbatim. No cmake -E env bash, no WINDOWS_ENGINE option.
